The temper is still on going, she finally can handle getting sent to time out in a peaceful way most the time. We suffer irreparable brain damage fairly quickly from lack of oxygen; only a few minutes IIRC. Is this normal for all cells or are neurons more fragile? Why can we stop/slow blood flow to our limbs (tourniquet for a wound) without them suffering drastic cell death?
Why do our brains die so fast?
I'm no neurologist, but I would assume it's because our brain has no fat or any other kind of energy reserve, so our brains can't anaerobically respire like other body parts can.
Thanks. And thanks to /u/Redeyedjedi for expanding on this guess.

/u/Satnavtomington is on target. First the brain has a high energy demand. Along with that it only has a singular energy source, sugar. It cannot utilize fatty acids for the production of energy. In addition to this the brain has a very small store of sugars for energy in the event that delivery of energy via the blood in the form sugar is interrupted. This suply is so small such that if blood sugars fall below 40 we begin to see serious dysfunction, even with ixygen available; the brain uses so much energy that even with a continuous supply it can run out if that supply stream is to little. Now without oxygen the brain can use anaerobic processes to produce energy, but this reduces the amount of energy produced by a factor of 4. Even with adequate delivery of augard sugar in such cases we get the metabolic derrangements that come with anaerobic metabolism the production of lactic acid being an example. The destruction of one cell and the products of apoptosis which it produces leads to damage of nieghboring cells and tissue and further demand for energy to remain viable (the exact process by which this occurs is not one which i recall off the top of my head and would have to search for)

The brain is always active, and always demanding energy. Another factor is the limited regenerative capacity of the brain, damage done is not going to be repaired.

Does anyone have any apps or tools that they use as a part of their daily practice that they'd like to recommend to others? Here are two that I find really handy:

  • Medigong (Android) - I've been using this for about a year, and it's a really good and simple meditation timer. You can set times for preparation before starting, intervals for awareness gong strokes, and end of meditation. You can also opt for 1 or 3 gongs to end the session. It's been great for meditation during lunch at work, or if I'm traveling. There's only one gong sound, but it's good at alerting you without being too jarring.
  • Daily Words of Buddha (Android) - Provides daily short verses from the Dhammapada in English, French, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, or Chinese, along with a link to the full source and the original pali. I mainly use the widget on my homescreen. Great for morning reflection/meditation.

Any other recommendations?

I prefer to keep things as simple as possible, if I don't need a thing I try and do without it. If I can replace something complex with something simple, I do so, rather than looking for things I don't need with the hope they will enhance my practice. If you're looking for apps to serve a specific purpose there are probably simpler ways to achieve the same ends.

That's a good point. In my case, I was looking for a meditation gong and a meditation timer. Since I already had the phone, it was simpler for me to download an app that could do both than to go out and purchase them separately.
